UTA.head: The Mammoth should be favored
UTA.body: Even though Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. If the Sharks want to spoil it, start with a power play that gets going.

SJS.head: A steep climb for the Sharks
SJS.body: Even though Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Sharks can start with a power play that gets going, plus Yaroslav Askarov stealing the show.

story.head: The Mammoth need a win
paras: The Mammoth are winless in four (0-2-2), and the Sharks (8-11-2) lost 3-2 in a shootout to Pittsburgh on Wednesday. Going in, the Sharks are fifth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Mammoth fifth in the Central (tied for 14th).

The Sharks’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth. The Mammoth have played better than their record (.550) says: their chances are worth about .697, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (31st), so the Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. San Jose has scored 2.43 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Mammoth, they rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (3rd). Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Macklin Celebrini (8 G / 15 A / 23 P in 19 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (5 G / 20 A / 25 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mikhail Sergachev (5 G / 15 A / 20 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind.

Yaroslav Askarov (5-8-1 / .894 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for San Jose. Utah has two options in net: Karel Vejmelka (6-6-1 / .876 SV% in 13 GS) and Sebastian Cossa (4-2-1 / .864 SV% in 7 GS). Vejmelka has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: The Sharks are newly without Alexander Wennberg, and have been without Igor Chernyshov since Oct 22.

The Mammoth are newly without Nate Schmidt, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche are missing more right now.
Tyler Toffoli has four goals in six games against Utah since 2023-24.
Vincent Trocheck is one assist from 400.
